title: Largest 3-Same-Digit Number in String
statement:
The string `num` is made of decimal digits. Look at every block of three consecutive characters of `num` in which all three characters are the same digit (such as `"444"`). Return the block with the greatest numeric value, as a string, or return `""` when `num` has no such block.

Leading zeros are allowed both in `num` and in the answer, so `"000"` is a valid answer.
notes:
## Intuition

There are only ten possible answers, `"000"` to `"999"`, so one option is to test them from the biggest down with a substring search. A single left-to-right pass does the same job directly: each position `i` ends a window of three characters, and the window is good when all three match. Because every candidate has exactly three identical digits, comparing two candidates as strings gives the same order as comparing them as numbers.

## Approach

1. Start with `best = ""` (no good block found yet).
2. For every index `i` from 2 to the end, check whether `num[i]`, `num[i - 1]` and `num[i - 2]` are equal.
3. If they are, cut out that `triple` and keep it if it is greater than `best`. The empty string is smaller than every triple, so the first one found always replaces it.
4. Return `best`, which is still `""` when no window matched.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = "6777133339"`. At `i = 3` the window `"777"` matches and beats `""`, so `best = "777"`. At `i = 7` the window `"333"` matches, but `"333" < "777"`; at `i = 8` `"333"` again, no change. No other window has three equal digits, so the answer is `"777"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per index (slicing three characters is constant).
- Space: O(1) besides the three-character strings.

## Pitfalls

- Return the string, not a number: `"000"` must stay `"000"`, not become `0` or `""`.
- A run longer than three, like `"0000"`, still contains good blocks; overlapping windows are fine.
- Do not return the first good block you meet; a later one may be larger.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | the largest good block found so far, or `""` |
| `i` | index of the last character of the current window |
| `triple` | the current window when its three digits match |

narration.2: No good block has been seen yet, so the answer starts as the empty string.
narration.3: Each index i from 2 on is the last character of a three-character window.
narration.4: The window is good only when all three characters are the same digit.
narration.5: Cut out the three matching characters.
narration.6: Same-digit triples compare as strings exactly as they do as numbers, and any triple beats the empty string.
narration.11: Return the largest good block, or the empty string if none was found.
